Hardening follow-ups

The hardening pass’s deferred items with their current status: the captive-DbContext, fire-and-forget-embedding, EF-baseline and plaintext-key items are resolved; unit-of-work beyond approve, analytics brush bindings, CancellationToken plumbing and DateTime.Kind remain open.

For Developers 1,030 words 5 min read windows-native/HARDENING-FOLLOWUPS.md ↗
follow-upstech debt

This file captures the deferred items from the Phase-7 multi-agent hardening pass. The applied fixes are in the commit that adds this file; the items below were intentionally not auto-fixed because they require a compiler to verify a non-trivial refactor, a public-API/DI change spanning layers, or a team decision.

Context: the pass was performed statically (no .NET SDK in the environment). Before release, build src/MemoryTimeline.sln with Visual Studio 2026 / msbuild (/t:Restore,Build /p:Platform=x64 — not dotnet build, which fails on the WinUI PRI task) and run the built test assembly with dotnet vstest, as CI does, to validate all applied fixes.

Status key (updated 2026-10-22): ✅ resolved · ⬜ still open (needs a decision or work).

High priority#

1. Captive / scope-captured DbContext (converged flag from 3 agents) — ✅ resolved#

TimelineViewModel is registered AddSingleton (App.xaml.cs) but depends on ITimelineService/IEventService (Scoped) → AppDbContext (Scoped). Pages also resolve their VMs from the root provider (App.Current.Services.GetRequiredService<…>), not from a DI scope. Net effect:

  • Production: a single AppDbContext lives for the whole app lifetime — not thread-safe, and the change-tracker grows unbounded.
  • Development (host scope validation): throws "Cannot consume scoped service from singleton."

Fix (coordinated, needs compile): register the context via AddDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>() and create a per-operation context in services, or resolve VMs/pages inside an explicit IServiceScope. Touches App DI + every repository/service ctor, so it was not done blind.

Resolution: App.xaml.cs registers AddDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>(); every repository and service opens a short-lived context per operation (await using var ctx = await _contextFactory.CreateDbContextAsync()) and is registered Singleton. This is now the data-access rule in claude.md.

2. EventService.CreateEventAsync fire-and-forget embedding (Core + Tests agents) — ✅ resolved#

_ = Task.Run(() => GenerateEmbeddingForEventAsync(createdEvent)) reuses the request-scoped AppDbContext on a background thread → ObjectDisposedException / "second operation on this context" once a real IEmbeddingService is registered. Currently masked by an internal catch (embeddings silently fail). Fix: inject IServiceScopeFactory, create a fresh scope+context for the background work (ctor change → flagged rather than applied).

Resolution: the shared-context Task.Run went away with the factory rework; the embedding path opens its own context per operation.

3. Migration + snapshot drift (Data agent — Critical for migration-based release) — ✅ resolved (2026-10-22)#

AppDbContextModelSnapshot is an empty stub and InitialCreate is far behind the model (missing tables era_categories, era_tags, milestones, saved_searches; missing columns on eras/events/tags; missing cross_references FKs; missing seed InsertData). Runtime is fine today because startup uses EnsureCreatedAsync() (schema built from the model), but any migration-based deploy will fail. Fix: on a machine with the SDK, regenerate the baseline (dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate --force) before shipping migrations.

Resolution (2026-10-22): a baseline migration (Data/Migrations/20261022004346_InitialCreate + snapshot; 25 tables, both seeds) was generated with dotnet ef through the new AppDbContextDesignTimeFactory, and SchemaUpgrader.EnsureSchemaAsync now runs Database.MigrateAsync. An unversioned database (built by EnsureCreated under an older build) is repaired by the idempotent DDL, baselined with InitialCreate (the history row is written through IHistoryRepository) and migrated forward; the first post-baseline migration is AddCaptureLocation. From here on a schema change ships as a migration only — the repair is frozen at the baseline shape (see claude.md, "Adding a feature").

Medium priority#

  • ✅ (approve path) / ⬜ (elsewhere) Unit-of-work / atomicity — multi-repository workflows (e.g. approve pending → create Event + delete PendingEvent) each call SaveChangesAsync independently and are not atomic. Introduce an explicit transaction / unit-of-work at the service layer. Approve is now one atomic transaction (event + tags/people/locations + pending-event delete); other multi-step workflows still save independently.
  • ✅ Polly referenced but unused — Core/Services/HttpRetryPolicy.cs (Polly 8 ResiliencePipeline: 3 retries, 500 ms exponential back-off with jitter, 4 s cap; retries transport errors, timeouts, 408/429/5xx, never caller cancellation or other 4xx) wraps the OpenAI-compatible LLM, OpenAI embeddings, Nominatim (no 429 retry) and the Anthropic SDK call.
  • ✅ CrossReference delete behavior = Restrict — the FK stays Restrict; EventRepository.DeleteAsync/DeleteRangeAsync remove the cross-references naming the event at either end in the same SaveChanges, proven by a file-backed SQLite test with PRAGMA foreign_keys on.
  • ✅ Analytics color bindings — CategoryDistribution/TagCloudItem/ActivityHeatmapCell.Color are hex strings; the four x:Bind Color sites in AnalyticsPage.xaml (category bars, tag cloud, person nodes, heatmap cells) now go through HexToBrushConverter, the project convention for every color that crosses the Core → view boundary (2026-10-22).

Low priority#

  • ✅ API keys stored plaintext in AppSettings — SettingsService stores the Anthropic key, embedding_api_key and the sync tokens through the ISecretProtector port (DpapiSecretProtector in the head: ProtectedData, CurrentUser scope, dpapi:v1: prefix); legacy plaintext rows are re-written in protected form on first read. A backup restored under another Windows account reads those secrets as empty and they must be re-entered. Keys can also be removed from Settings ("Clear key" / Reset to Defaults).
  • ✅ CancellationToken not plumbable — resolved in the same change set (2026-10-22): every repository method takes CancellationToken cancellationToken = default and passes it to EF, and the Sync callers forward theirs; on the Core side queue processing (ProcessNextItemAsync / ProcessAllPendingAsync) takes a token that reaches the Whisper decode and the extraction model call, so a cancelled item goes back to Pending instead of failing.
  • ⬜ DateTime.Kind round-trip — SQLite returns Unspecified; a UTC ValueConverter on DateTime properties would avoid local/UTC comparison bugs. Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.Pre10TimeZoneHandling is pinned at both entry points (app and tests) so stored values keep reading as they were written. Owner decision needed before anything changes: either (a) add the UTC converter and audit/convert the values already stored under the old rules (a one-off data migration of every DateTime column — user databases hold both local and UTC values today), or (b) keep the pre-10 switch pinned indefinitely and document Unspecified as the contract. Until that call is made, no code change is planned here.
  • ✅ Inclusive viewport boundaries — closed: inclusive is intended. The predicate the timeline actually renders with is TimelineCoordinateConverter.IsRangeVisible (closed on both ends, matching the data layer's overlap query, so an edge-touching event is loaded and drawn consistently); the decision is recorded on it and on TimelineViewport.IsEventVisible. EventLayoutEngine / EventLayout.cs had no production caller and were deleted together with EventLayoutEngineTests.cs (2026-10).
  • ✅ Singleton AnthropicLlmService caches _model at first init — a later model change in settings needs an app restart. Resolved: RoutingLlmService is the registered ILlmService and re-reads provider/model/key on every call, so Settings changes apply live.
